status_summary: H.R. 1602, the Financial Privacy Act of 2025, was reported by the House Financial Services Committee on 2025-03-21; per the CBO estimate of 2025-03-31 it would require FinCEN to report annually to Congress on the number and types of suspicious activity reports, a narrower step than the public data on reports, prosecutions, fines and costs the chapter asks for. FinCEN published a proposed rule on anti-money laundering programs on 2026-04-10, citing Executive Order 14192 and aiming to reduce compliance burdens; it does not require the annual data, the FinCEN and GAO evaluations, or the retrospective review the chapter describes. Committee leaders urged FinCEN on 2026-06-09 to finalize that rule with reduced burdens.

timeline.event: The House Financial Services Committee reported H.R. 1602, which would require FinCEN to report annually to Congress on the number and types of suspicious activity reports (CBO estimate dated 2025-03-31).
FinCEN published a proposed rule reforming anti-money laundering program requirements and citing regulatory burden reduction.
House Financial Services Committee Republican leaders sent FinCEN a letter urging a final rule with reduced compliance burdens and higher report filing thresholds (reported 2026-06-26).

title: Publish annual AML data and require a retrospective review of FinCEN rules
uncertainties: The H.R. 1602 provisions come from the CBO description, not the bill text, and later floor action was not checked. The proposed rule was read in full through two passes and contains no data publication or retrospective review requirement. The FinCEN SAR statistics page prints no date and was not treated as evidence. A letter from legislators is listed because it was a dated official act, though it does not advance the specific items.
